title: Freeze time across a multi-step billing flow
description: Tests a monthly billing close job that depends on several time boundaries.
code:
def test_billing_close(service):
    service.create_invoice('acct-1')
    service.run_close_job()
    summary = service.monthly_summary('acct-1')
    assert summary['period'] == '2026-05'
    assert summary['closed_at'] == '2026-05-31T23:59:59Z'
issue_title: Test relies on uncontrolled wall-clock behavior
issue_description: Without freezing time, period boundaries and close timestamps become flaky and difficult to reproduce.
issue_suggestion: Use a frozen clock for the entire workflow and assert against the controlled instant.

title: Assert retry exhaustion and dead-letter behavior
description: Covers a worker that retries failed jobs and then dead-letters them.
code:
def test_worker_failure(worker, queue):
    queue.push({'id': 'job-1'})
    worker.run_once()
    assert queue.size() == 0
issue_title: Test ignores the terminal retry path
issue_description: A worker can appear to process the queue while still mishandling retry counts or dead-letter routing.
issue_suggestion: Drive the job through all retry attempts and assert the final dead-letter outcome explicitly.

title: Verify ordering guarantees in concurrent consumers
description: Exercises a queue consumer that should preserve per-account ordering.
code:
def test_account_events(consumer, queue):
    queue.push({'account_id': 'a1', 'seq': 1})
    queue.push({'account_id': 'a1', 'seq': 2})
    consumer.drain()
    assert consumer.processed_count() == 2
issue_title: The test misses the ordering contract
issue_description: Counting processed events does not prove they were applied in the required sequence for the same account.
issue_suggestion: Assert the observed order for the account-specific event stream.

title: Prove idempotency under duplicate submissions
description: Tests an order-create endpoint that may receive the same idempotency key twice.
issue_title: The test codifies duplicate creation instead of idempotency
issue_description: Systems with idempotency keys should prove the duplicate request does not create a second side effect.
issue_suggestion: Send the same request with one idempotency key and assert only one order exists.

title: Cover rollback behavior after partial persistence
description: Tests a service that writes a DB row before publishing an event.
code:
def test_signup(service, db, bus):
    bus.fail_next_publish()
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        service.signup('a@example.com')
    assert db.users.count() == 1
issue_title: Test expects partial success after failure
issue_description: If the workflow should be atomic, keeping the user row after publish failure is the bug, not the contract.
issue_suggestion: Assert that the transaction rolled back or compensation cleaned up the partial write.

title: Validate redaction in structured error logs
description: Exercises a failure path that logs the outbound request body.
code:
def test_payment_error(logger, service):
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        service.charge({'card_number': '4111111111111111', 'cvv': '123'})
    assert logger.error.called
issue_title: Sensitive values in logs are not checked
issue_description: The test passes even if raw PAN or CVV data is emitted into structured logs.
issue_suggestion: Assert that the logged payload is redacted before it reaches the logger sink.

title: Assert cache invalidation after a write
description: Tests a profile update flow that also invalidates a cached summary.
issue_description: The test proves the canonical record updated but not that dependent caches were invalidated.
issue_suggestion: Assert the invalidation or refreshed cache state after the mutation.

title: Exercise optimistic lock conflicts
description: Covers an update endpoint backed by a version column.
issue_description: Versioned writes need a test for stale updates, not just the happy path.
issue_suggestion: Add a stale-version request and assert a conflict response or retry behavior.

title: Verify webhook signature failures do not process side effects
description: Tests a webhook handler that should reject bad signatures before enqueuing work.
issue_description: A bad-signature response is not sufficient if the handler still enqueued internal work before failing.
issue_suggestion: Assert the queue or persistence layer remains untouched when verification fails.

title: Prove scheduler behavior across daylight-saving boundaries
description: Tests a reminder scheduler keyed to local user time.
issue_description: Local-time schedulers often break around DST transitions even when the nominal hour assertion passes.
issue_suggestion: Add a DST boundary case and assert the next_run semantics across the transition.
